explain.text: Brand Visibility measures how your brand appears in AI-generated answers, recommends content changes and tracks how that performance changes over time.
Brand Visibility measures how your brand appears in AI-generated answers.

Brand Visibility runs the prompts you choose on a recurring basis across the AI platforms it supports and records how your brand appears in each answer and how that changes over time. It measures the prompts you monitor: the questions people put to AI assistants themselves are not disclosed by the platforms.

Adobe's Brand Presence page lists ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and Perplexity as supported. The experience varies with your Brand Visibility edition, so we would confirm the platforms in yours before the baseline.
explain.confirm: Brand Visibility platforms: the list of six with Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot is on one of Adobe's Brand Presence pages; the AI Visibility page lists ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode and Gemini, and the Brand Presence (powered by Semrush) page names none. Confirm with Adobe which platforms your client's edition covers before you promise Perplexity.

explain.text: Its AI Visibility view opens the full AI answer behind a prompt: the response text, whether your brand was mentioned, which other brands were mentioned, whether your site was cited and the source URLs behind the answer.

The dashboards report the percentage of prompts where your brand is mentioned, how often your website is used as a source, share of voice and sentiment, and compare you with the other brands you choose to track in each market.

Two further views cover your own site: Agentic Traffic shows how AI agents (crawlers and chatbots) interact with your pages, from your CDN logs, and Referral Traffic shows the visits from people who clicked citation links in AI-generated answers.
Brand Concierge is Adobe's platform for conversational experiences on your website, mobile apps and other digital properties. Every conversation is grounded in your own content and guardrails.
Brand Concierge answers visitors' questions from the content you approve.

Brand Concierge answers only from the knowledge sources you configure (website pages, PDFs and product spreadsheets), not from general world knowledge. Website sources refresh on a schedule you set, so answers keep up with the pages you publish.

When a question falls outside those sources, the concierge is designed to say it does not have the information rather than generate an unsupported answer, and guardrails can exclude topics such as legal or compliance matters.

Brand Concierge is focused on anonymous visitors: it answers from the conversation and your knowledge sources, not from an individual customer's records. Questions about a customer's own account would go to your secure channels.
explain.confirm: Brand Concierge and a customer's own account: Adobe's FAQ says the current scope is anonymous visitors, while other Adobe pages mention account information and a Real-Time CDP integration that only some customers have. Do not promise answers about an individual customer's account until Adobe confirms it.

explain.text: Before launch, it is tested against a golden set of real customer questions paired with ideal answers, including questions it should not answer; after launch, conversation transcripts are reviewed on a recurring basis.
A conversation can be handed to a person through live chat or a booked meeting without losing its context; both run on Adobe's companion product, Adobe Marketo Qualifier.
explain.confirm: Brand Concierge handoff: live chat and meeting booking run on Adobe Marketo Qualifier (formerly Sales Qualifier), which Adobe frames as handoff to sales. Confirm with Adobe that your client has access to it and that it suits a service handoff.

Brand Concierge handoff: live chat and meeting booking run on Adobe Marketo Qualifier (formerly Sales Qualifier), which Adobe frames as handoff to sales. Confirm with Adobe that your client has access to it and that it suits a service handoff.

explain.text: AEM Sites as a Cloud Service is built on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, with code deployed through Cloud Manager and pages edited visually in the Universal Editor.
AEM Sites is where the site is built, on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, and where your authors edit its pages.
We would implement AEM Sites as a Cloud Service. Code is deployed through Cloud Manager, Adobe's one route for it, so every release passes the same code quality checks.
We would start with discovery: a review of your current site's content, templates and integrations, a named team with agreed roles, and the measures of success.

asks.text: Access to your client's current site and its content, or an export of it.
asks.client: Access to the current site and its content, or an export of it.

asks.text: An inventory of your client's pages, URLs and integrations, with an owner for each content area.
asks.client: An inventory of pages, URLs and integrations, with an owner for each content area.

asks.text: Named reviewers at your client for the content checks and user acceptance testing.
asks.client: Named reviewers for the content checks and user acceptance testing.

asks.text: Your client's accessibility, retention and security requirements for the site.
asks.client: Your accessibility, retention and security requirements for the site.

explain.text: How your existing content moves depends on where it sits today. From an existing AEM instance, Adobe's Content Transfer Tool moves it across. From another CMS, we would export the content, map it to the new templates and load it into AEM, agreeing the mapping and tooling with you in discovery.
explain.confirm: AEM Sites migration from another CMS: Adobe documents the Content Transfer Tool for AEM sources only (AEM 6.3 or higher), and the AEM Importer and the Experience Modernization Agent for Edge Delivery Services targets only. Ask your client what the site runs on today before you size the migration.

explain.text: For go-live we would plan a content freeze for the final content top-up, check the migrated content with you, test in the stage environment, which has the same sizing as production, and run user acceptance testing on a test subdomain before the DNS cutover, with redirects for retired URLs and rollback criteria agreed beforehand.

There are two documented routes. The simpler one: forms built in Marketo Engage are embedded on the site's pages with Marketo's own embed code, so each submission is a Marketo form fill. We would place the embed in a reusable page component, agree the fields, consent wording and validation with you, and collect only the data you approve. Marketo's form prefill does not work with the embed code.
licensing: Embedded Marketo forms: your Marketo Engage subscription, with no AEM Forms license.
Adaptive forms with the Submit to Marketo Engage action: a Marketo Engage license and an AEM Forms license, since AEM Sites and AEM Forms are licensed individually.

explain.text: The fuller one: AEM Forms adaptive forms with the Submit to Marketo Engage action, which add a rule editor, prefill and a PDF record of each submission, and can connect to Adobe Sign for e-signatures. We would use embedded Marketo forms for standard lead capture and adaptive forms where a form needs that logic.
licensing: Embedded Marketo forms: your Marketo Engage subscription, with no AEM Forms license.
Adaptive forms with the Submit to Marketo Engage action: a Marketo Engage license and an AEM Forms license, since AEM Sites and AEM Forms are licensed individually.

explain.text: Real-Time CDP brings known and anonymous data from your systems together into customer profiles, builds audiences from them and activates those audiences across channels.
Real-Time CDP brings known and anonymous customer data together into profiles and builds the audiences.

Adobe Target personalizes experiences across web, mobile and other digital channels: A/B tests compare experiences, and Experience Targeting delivers content to a specific audience by rules you define.
Target delivers the personalized experiences on the site and tests them.
Customer Journey Analytics brings Analysis Workspace to the data in Adobe Experience Platform, so journeys can be analyzed across channels in one reporting view.
Customer Journey Analytics measures the results across channels.

In Customer Journey Analytics your data can be viewed and analyzed in sequence across channels: data from your call center, point-of-sale systems and online properties is combined into a single reporting view.
A customer becomes known when they sign in: the site sends a person-level identifier, such as a CRM ID or a hashed email, with the visit, and Experience Platform stitches it into their profile.
Real-Time CDP's Adobe Target destination makes those audiences available to Target for same-page and next-page personalization, with governance and privacy support, using a datastream.

Results are measured in Customer Journey Analytics, used as the reporting source for Target's A/B activities: its Experimentation panel compares the variations and reports each one's lift over the baseline, and the confidence in it, on the success metrics you choose.
explain.confirm: Target reporting in Customer Journey Analytics: it covers A/B activities. Auto-Target and Automated Personalization cannot use Customer Journey Analytics as the reporting source, and Automated Personalization and Recommendations need Target Premium. Check which activity types your client wants before you promise this reporting for them.

explain.text: Consent and data-use rules travel with the data: the Web SDK sends or discards data according to each visitor's consent, and Experience Platform enforces the data usage policies you enable when audiences are activated. We would keep sensitive attributes out of those audiences unless you approve them, and never use personalization to decide eligibility or pricing.

Journey Optimizer is Adobe's application for creating and delivering connected, personalized customer experiences across your channels. It is built on Adobe Experience Platform and its real-time customer profile, and runs both real-time journeys and scheduled campaigns.
Journey Optimizer orchestrates the journeys and campaigns and delivers the messages across channels.

We would set Journey Optimizer up in the order Adobe documents: the environment first, with a development sandbox for building and testing and a production sandbox for sending, each with its own channel configurations. Journeys are tested with test profiles before activation.

A journey automates a real-time, multi-step sequence of interactions; a campaign sends a scheduled or API-triggered message to an audience. Messages are delivered through channels like email, mobile messages, push notifications and direct mail.
Journey Optimizer tracks customer engagement and campaign performance with reports, and its reporting is integrated with Customer Journey Analytics for a clearer view of performance metrics.

When messages are sent from journeys or campaigns, your customers must always be able to unsubscribe; once they do, their profiles are automatically removed from the audience of future marketing messages. Access labels control which users can reach specific journeys, campaigns and channel configurations.

Journey Optimizer B2B Edition orchestrates person and account journeys for marketing-qualified buying groups. Account journeys move accounts through the journey, not people, and the product is built on Adobe Experience Platform, including Real-Time CDP B2B.
Journey Optimizer B2B Edition runs the account journeys and the buying groups.

A buying group is the subset of people in an account who make the purchase decision. An account journey splits its paths on account, people or buying group criteria, and on each path actions send communications or wait for an event to occur.

Experience Platform is the primary data store for accounts, people and opportunities, and audiences are built with Real-Time CDP account segmentation. A dedicated Marketo Engage instance provides email delivery, so we would configure email tracking and deliverability there and in the B2B Edition app.

Your existing Marketo Engage instances can be connected as well: journey actions coordinate the account-based journeys with lead-based campaigns in Marketo Engage, such as adding people to a list or a request campaign.
Its Intelligent Dashboard provides a comprehensive view of buying group and account metrics, to monitor your marketing efforts.
Experimentation Accelerator integrates with Adobe Target and Adobe Journey Optimizer to give you a centralized platform for managing, analyzing and optimizing your experiments.
Experimentation Accelerator tracks the tests from Adobe Target and Journey Optimizer in one place and recommends what to test next.

Its Experiments tab centralizes the tracking and analysis of tests from Adobe Journey Optimizer and Adobe Target, with their KPIs. For each experiment it identifies the treatment currently delivering the best performance and measures its percentage improvement over the control or baseline.

Each experiment carries a hypothesis: the planned changes to be tested and their expected impact on the primary metric. The Opportunities panel then displays AI-generated recommendations designed to enhance test performance and align with your broader business objectives.

Experimentation Accelerator only makes recommendations: it has no access to modify test settings, and every recommendation can be reviewed and edited before it is pushed out. A dedicated model is trained for every sandbox, using only your own data.

Content Analytics shows how your content affects the key performance indicators you have defined. It breaks content down into components and attributes, so you can analyze what content, and what attributes of that content, drive business results.
Content Analytics measures which content, and which attributes of that content, drive business results.

We would set Content Analytics up with Adobe's guided configuration wizard, which covers all the steps required. The Experience Platform Web or Mobile SDK then records impressions and interactions with your content, and data collection starts once the Tags property is published.

Reporting is in Customer Journey Analytics, where a Workspace template gives you a pre-populated project with content insights: which assets are receiving impressions and where, and engagement such as the average click through rate for assets with certain attributes.
Access is governed through data views: a user or group of users reaches Content Analytics only through the data views that are configured for it.

Marketing Campaign Analytics measures your campaigns and optimizes planning holistically across all your channels. It provides the incremental impact of your marketing activities on business and campaign outcomes, for digital and offline marketing.
Marketing Campaign Analytics measures the incremental impact of your marketing across channels and plans the budget.

It works with event level data and with aggregate or summary data such as offline advertising. We would ingest that data, configure the mapping and conflict resolution rules that merge your marketing datasets, then build models that measure and predict the outcome you specify.

Its marketing mix modeling is a privacy-friendly machine learning analysis of the incremental impact of marketing tactics and business factors on conversion metrics. Transfer learning unifies it with multi-touch attribution, so measurement and planning give consistent results.
Plans allocate budgets by business unit and channel, using the outcomes of the trained models. You can develop multiple budget plans and compare their impact before you decide.
Access is controlled through Experience Platform, in the Adobe Admin Console and through Permissions.

Real-Time CDP Collaboration lets you discover, activate and measure high-value audiences with advertisers and publishers, without relying on third-party cookies, in a privacy-centric, centralized environment.
Real-Time CDP Collaboration matches your audiences with those of advertisers and publishers for discovery, activation and measurement.

Setup starts with access roles, which determine what your users can see and do. We would define your account's role, provide your branding assets, configure the match keys that align audiences across connections and select the consent mode that determines which profiles are eligible.

Work with each collaborator runs in projects: audience overlap calculations, discovering relevant audiences, activating audiences and measuring campaign performance. You see the overlap percentages and the number of overlapping identities between your audiences and theirs, and campaign performance in simplified and customizable reports.

Embedded controls guide the responsible use of audience data at every step of your workflows, and a consent mode of opt-in, opt-out or none determines which profiles are eligible to be included in connections.

Adobe Analytics gathers data from your digital customer interactions and turns it into actionable insights, with in-depth analysis and versatile reporting. Its Analysis Workspace is a drag-and-drop interface for building analyses and sharing them.
Adobe Analytics collects the data from your website and apps and reports on it.

Adobe Analytics needs code in your website or app to send it data. We would start from a solution design document, the blueprint that translates what your stakeholders need into Analytics variables, and implement with the Web SDK extension, Adobe's standardized and recommended method.
Reporting is in Analysis Workspace: analyses are built by drag and drop, visualizations bring the data to life, and projects can be shared and scheduled with anyone you choose.

Access is governed by product profiles, permission presets that your product admins assign to users, and by report suites: a user must belong to at least one report suite to be given access to Adobe Analytics.
Data feeds deliver the raw data out of Adobe Analytics in hourly or daily batches, for use in your other platforms, and the A4T integration brings Adobe Analytics and Adobe Target together.

Marketo Measure is a marketing attribution solution: it automatically tracks and reports on channel performance, showing which marketing efforts are the most effective in driving revenue, so you can optimize your marketing spend.
Marketo Measure attributes revenue credit to the marketing channels and touchpoints.

We would add the Marketo Measure JavaScript to all your web properties, where it tracks online marketing interactions, called touchpoints. The standard installation puts a Salesforce Package or a Microsoft Dynamics Managed Solution in your CRM, where the captured data is housed and organized.

Attribution assigns revenue credit to marketing touchpoints by tracking the whole journey, from a prospect's first interaction with your company to when the deal closes. Marketo Measure offers six types of attribution models, from simple single-touch models to more complex multi-touch models.

Its ROI Dashboard gives a granular view of returns on investment across channels, subchannels and campaigns. Spend data is key to that reporting, so we would make sure the appropriate spend data for each of your channels is pulled into Marketo Measure.

Edge Delivery Services is Adobe's content delivery framework, a core part of Adobe Experience Manager, built for speed, simplicity and scalability. It works with your own CDN or the included Adobe-managed CDN.
Edge Delivery Services delivers the site's pages, built for speed.
We would build the site on Edge Delivery Services with its code managed and deployed directly from a GitHub repository. New content is added instantly, without a rebuild process.

Every project on Edge Delivery Services should produce a Lighthouse score of 100 for mobile and desktop, measured with Google PageSpeed Insights. Adobe's guidance is that the score is not hard to keep at 100 with continuous testing, so we would test each change.
explain.confirm: Edge Delivery Services performance: the Lighthouse score of 100 is what Adobe's go-live checklist says a project should produce, not a guarantee, and the same page warns that a CDN layer can lower it. Do not promise the score in a contract.

explain.text: Your authors can work in AEM Authoring, which includes Document Authoring and AEM Sites Author, or in Microsoft SharePoint or Google Drive. They get an instant URL to see their content changes and share them with others for review.
explain.confirm: Edge Delivery Services authoring: Adobe's overview now names Experience Workspace as the default for new projects and the Universal Editor for existing AEM implementations. Agree the authoring method with your client and Adobe before you describe it.

explain.text: For your existing site, Adobe's importer automates importing and converting multiple pages. We would make example imports of each page type so your authors can confirm the structure, and reflect retired URLs in the redirects spreadsheet.

Sites Optimizer is Adobe's cloud-based service that analyzes and improves the performance of websites built on AEM. Each opportunity it finds shows the potential business value and gives actionable recommendations.
Sites Optimizer analyzes the site and recommends improvements to its performance.

For search traffic, Sites Optimizer identifies external links that point to non-existent pages on your site and missing or faulty metadata on your pages. Its Google Search Console connector adds search rankings, click-through rates and Core Web Vitals to the analysis.
explain.confirm: Sites Optimizer metadata fixes: Adobe's page marks deploying the metadata fixes automatically as Sites Optimizer Ultimate, and the Google Search Console connector needs credentials with administrative access to Search Console for the domain. Check your client's Sites Optimizer package and who holds that access.

explain.text: Sites Optimizer continuously monitors site performance, using Operational Telemetry to detect regressions in Core Web Vitals. Its code updates follow standard development practices, with review and approval before anything is merged into production.
explain.confirm: Sites Optimizer and Core Web Vitals: Adobe's page says only pages with at least 1000 page views can be analyzed, and the fixes arrive as pull requests on the site's code repository, which must be connected first.

explain.text: Sites Optimizer applies the optimizations you select into the authoring environment only. Your AEM authors then review and publish the changes from the CMS.
Its site summary gives a snapshot of your site's performance, how Sites Optimizer has improved the site over time and the opportunities for improvement that remain.

AEM Assets as a Cloud Service is Adobe's cloud-native solution for digital asset management and Dynamic Media. It helps you maximize the value of your digital assets across creation, management and delivery.
AEM Assets is the repository where your digital assets are managed, enriched and delivered.

To bring your existing library across, Bulk Import lets administrators import large numbers of assets directly from an external data source in a single operation. AEM applies smart tags to uploaded assets automatically, by default.

People find the right asset through smart tags, customized metadata and enhanced search. Metadata forms let you add your own business-specific fields to an asset's details page, and we would agree those fields with you before the assets are loaded.
For distribution, Content Hub centralizes and distributes approved brand and marketing content. Only assets marked Approved in AEM Assets become available there.
explain.confirm: AEM Assets Content Hub: Adobe calls Content Hub an add-on for AEM Assets as a Cloud Service. It is enabled through Cloud Manager and, once enabled on a production environment, cannot be disabled in a self-service manner. Confirm your client is entitled to it before you propose it.

explain.text: Asset reports show how the system is used, how users interact with assets and which assets are shared.

AEM Forms as a Cloud Service is Adobe's cloud-native solution to create, manage, publish and update complex digital forms, integrating the submitted data with your back-end processes and business rules and saving it in an external data store.
AEM Forms provides the digital forms and integrates what people submit with your back-end processes.
We would build your forms on Adaptive Forms Core Components, which Adobe recommends for new forms. Rules then trigger actions on form fields based on conditions, user inputs and user actions.

We would connect the forms to your data sources, so customer data is fetched while a form renders and submitted data is written back to update those sources. Submit actions can also send form data to services such as OneDrive, SharePoint and Workfront Fusion.

Forms-centric workflows route form data to managers or departments for review, approval or further processing, with consistent and auditable processing and role-based access control. Adobe Acrobat Sign adds e-signature workflows, and submitted forms can be archived as PDF files.
explain.confirm: AEM Forms e-signatures: signing goes through Adobe Acrobat Sign, which is its own product and license, and Adobe's page lists an Acrobat Sign developer account and API application as prerequisites. Confirm your client has Acrobat Sign before you promise e-signatures on forms.

explain.text: AEM Forms integrates with Adobe Analytics to capture and track performance metrics for your published forms, so you can see interaction patterns and the problems people face while using them.
explain.confirm: AEM Forms analytics: the form metrics come from Adobe Analytics, which is its own product and license. Confirm your client has Adobe Analytics before you promise form reporting.

explain.text: Adobe Commerce is Adobe's B2B and B2C commerce platform for digital commerce experiences across online and physical spaces. Its Admin gives your team marketing, search engine optimization and product management tools.
Adobe Commerce runs the store: products, promotions and orders are managed in its Admin.

We would follow Adobe's implementation playbook for Commerce projects, which sets out methodologies and best practices from the early stages of project scoping through development, integrations and deployment to ongoing support.

For business buyers, Adobe Commerce B2B accommodates companies with complex organizational structures and multiple users with various roles and levels of purchasing permission. Shared catalogs set custom prices per product for different companies.
explain.confirm: Adobe Commerce B2B: Adobe's Admin user guides mark Adobe Commerce B2B as PaaS only (Adobe Commerce on Cloud and on-premises projects). Check which Commerce deployment your client has, or is buying, before you promise company accounts and shared catalogs.

explain.text: Live Search replaces the standard search in Adobe Commerce. Product Recommendations use Adobe AI and machine learning, trained on aggregated shopper behavior and catalog data, to deliver personalized recommendations on the storefront.
explain.confirm: Adobe Commerce Product Recommendations: Adobe says the service is not HIPAA-ready and must not be used where protected health information is processed, and it asks you to review Live Search's boundaries and limits before implementation. Check both against your client's catalog and industry.

explain.text: The Data Connection extension connects your Adobe Commerce web instance to Adobe Experience Platform and the Edge Network. It collects behavioral storefront data from the browser, back office data from the Commerce servers and profile data.
Marketo Engage is Adobe's marketing automation platform, a single solution that lets you attract, segment and nurture your customers. Each marketing initiative runs as a program.
Marketo Engage runs the marketing programs that attract, segment and nurture your customers.

We would configure the admin settings, including CNAMEs and Marketo's JavaScript tracking code, Munchkin, which tracks the people who visit your website so that automated campaigns can react to their visits. We would test the automation workflows and the data sync before launch.
explain.confirm: Marketo web tracking: Adobe says Munchkin tracks anonymous visitors too, along with their IP addresses and other information. Agree with your client how that sits with their cookie consent and privacy notice before the tracking code goes on the site.

explain.text: Campaigns run as Smart Campaigns. A Smart List defines who you want to target, using filters and triggers, and the flow sets the steps the campaign performs, including wait steps and split choices.

Where your CRM is Salesforce, the sync is bidirectional for leads, contacts and Salesforce campaigns, so a change made in either system is reflected in both. All other syncs run from Salesforce to Marketo only.
explain.confirm: Marketo CRM sync: this sentence describes the Salesforce sync only. Marketo documents a separate sync for Microsoft Dynamics, and Adobe says the first Salesforce sync may take hours or even days. Ask which CRM your client runs before you use it.

explain.text: Marketo's reports include email performance, covering delivered or bounced, opened, clicked and unsubscribed, and landing page performance, covering visits, conversions and other metrics.
Adobe Acrobat converts, edits, shares and signs PDFs. The Acrobat Services APIs automate the generation, manipulation and transformation of document content through cloud-based web services.
Acrobat and Acrobat Services convert, edit and automate your PDF documents.

With the PDF Services API we would automate document steps such as creating a PDF from a dynamic HTML report, setting a password to prevent unauthorized opening, compressing it for sharing, or extracting text, tables, images and document structure for downstream solutions.
explain.confirm: Acrobat Services processing region: Adobe's page says PDF Services processes documents in the United States by default and that the European region (Ireland) can be chosen call by call. Agree the region with your client before any document is sent to the API.

explain.text: With the Document Generation API we would merge your data with Word templates to create documents such as contracts, invoices, proposals and reports. The PDF Electronic Seal API can apply an electronic seal, using your organization's digital certificate, to demonstrate their integrity and authenticity.
explain.confirm: Acrobat Services electronic seals: the seal uses a digital certificate issued to your client by a Trust Service Provider that Adobe supports. Confirm they have one, or plan for getting it.

explain.text: The PDF Accessibility Auto-Tag API adds document structure tags that assistive technology uses to read a PDF, and can be applied at scale to large backlogs. Its output is not guaranteed to comply fully with WCAG and PDF/UA, so we would review and remediate afterwards.
The PDF Embed API brings PDF viewing into your web applications with a few lines of JavaScript, with support for commenting, drawing, highlighting and text editing tools.

Acrobat Sign is Adobe's digital signature service, which lets people sign documents electronically and lets you collect signatures. It scales to your organization's needs with integrations, APIs and advanced authentication.
Acrobat Sign collects the electronic signatures on your documents.

We would set up reusable document templates in your Acrobat Sign library, which provide speed and consistency and let you manage document revisions, and custom workflows that speed up creating and sending an agreement.

A web form lets people sign a document electronically directly on your website, through a hosted link or embedded in the page. With bulk sending, everyone gets their own document to sign and you can track each person's progress.

Every document in Acrobat Sign passes through a series of milestones, which are documented in an audit report for every transaction. Reports can show the percentage of agreements signed and the average time it takes to sign.
explain.confirm: Acrobat Sign reporting: Adobe's tutorial notes that reporting, like groups, is only available for business and enterprise-level plans. Check your client's Acrobat Sign plan before you promise reports.

explain.text: Acrobat Sign can be used inside applications your organization already uses, such as Microsoft, Salesforce and Workday. Its features are also available through REST APIs.
explain.confirm: Acrobat Sign integrations: Adobe's integrations page asks users to check with their administrator that an integration is enabled. Name only the integrations your client's account has enabled or will enable.

explain.text: Workfront is Adobe's suite of cloud-based applications for planning, project management, collaboration and resource management. It organizes, prioritizes, tracks and manages both your work and your resources.
Workfront organizes, prioritizes, tracks and manages the work and its resources.

We would set up request queues, so every request is submitted the same way and follows the same path to completion, with routing rules that send each one to a user, job role, team or project, and project templates that capture your repeatable processes.
Reviews and approvals can be one-time or come from reusable approval templates, with multi-stage approvals and parallel paths, and comprehensive audit logging keeps a complete governance trail.
Workfront organizes information in reports, places multiple reports on a dashboard and lets you share both reports and dashboards with others.
Access is governed at two levels: your Workfront administrator sets the access levels, and within those levels people share objects with view, contribute or manage permissions.

Workfront Planning gives you visibility into the operational details of your organization. You decide which record types you use, such as campaigns, and how they link to one another and to object types from other systems.
Workfront Planning gives visibility into the operational details of your organization, in record types you define and link to one another.

We would build your workspaces from a predefined template or with your own record types and fields, and define how the record types relate to one another. Each record type can have a request form, so people add records by submitting it.
Records open in a table view by default, and you can also create a timeline or a calendar view of them.

Record types connect to one another and to objects from other applications. A campaign record type connected to a Workfront project can bring the project's planned completion date onto the record. Each connected application needs its own license and account.
You share workspaces with users, groups, teams, companies and job roles. Sharing a workspace also shares its record types, records and fields; views are shared separately.
Frame.io is where your creative teams and their stakeholders organize, review and manage creative assets as they move from ideation to final approval.
Frame.io is where creative assets are organized, reviewed and managed on their way to final approval.

Reviewers and approvers add comments, mark up the asset and make the approval decision in the Frame.io viewer, which provides version history and comparison and time-stamped comments for video reviews.

Each user has an account role, assigned in the Adobe Admin Console, that sets their baseline permissions: Content Admins have administrative access to all public resources, and Members need an explicit invitation to reach a project or workspace.
Frame.io has a REST API and webhooks for custom workflows and automations, and server-to-server authentication integrates it with your other tools without relying on individual user accounts.
Adobe Express is where your teams create and edit images and videos for social posts, flyers, logos and more, from shared templates whose style controls keep them on brand.
Adobe Express lets your teams create content from shared templates that keep them on brand.

We would set up your brands in Adobe Express with their logos, colors, fonts, graphics and guidelines, then apply style controls to the templates you share, which restrict teams to approved colors and fonts.

Roles and permissions are managed through the Admin Console, so your Enterprise admins give every team member the right level of access. Capabilities such as creating or editing templates and publishing to social media can be disabled for members.
Shareable templates can carry a review and approval workflow: approvers you name from your account, or an advanced review that sends Adobe Express files to Workfront for review.
Adobe Express shows analytics for your custom templates, so you can see how often they are being discovered and reused, and download them as CSV.

Creative Cloud gives your teams access to Adobe's collection of software for graphic design, video editing, web development and photography, with cloud services. Product profiles decide who has access to which apps and services.
Creative Cloud provides the design apps your creative teams work in, such as Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign.

We would deploy the apps with managed packages, which control which Adobe applications and versions are deployed and when updates are applied, and assign people to product profiles that match access to your roles, departments or teams.

Asset settings give you control over how people share company-owned assets externally: a system administrator can restrict sharing features so that sensitive content reaches only appropriate external recipients.

Creative Cloud Libraries let your creative teams capture, organize and share design elements. A library of corporate colors, type styles, logos and other brand assets can be view-only, so designers always have the most up-to-date assets.

Designers reach content stored in Experience Manager Assets through the Adobe Asset Link panel in InDesign, Photoshop and Illustrator, without leaving the apps, and can open their Workfront projects directly from the same three apps.
GenStudio for Performance Marketing is an application built on Adobe's generative AI platform. It lets your marketing teams create, manage and optimize campaign content for ads and email.
GenStudio for Performance Marketing creates and optimizes the campaign content for ads and email.

We would start with your brand guidelines, which the generative AI uses as guardrails that guide content generation, and with templates that contain approved features and are optimized for specific channels.

Activation takes an approved ad experience and its assets, applies the setup the channel requires and delivers it directly to a channel such as Meta or LinkedIn in an inactive status, for your final review in the channel's own ad manager.

Once a channel account is connected, Insights receives data from your active campaigns, media and ads and provides analytics on content performance. You can find content that is not performing well and create variations of it with the integrated generative AI.

Editors create campaign assets, request content review and approval and publish the approved drafts; collaborators view and approve content. With Workfront Proof, the review gains approval templates, multi-stage workflows and proof version comparison.

Coworker is Adobe's AI-powered teammate for customer experience and marketing workflows. You describe a goal in plain language, and it plans the work, executes it across your Adobe and connected systems, validates the results and brings the finished work back for your approval.
Coworker lets your teams ask for insights, content and actions across your Adobe applications in natural language.

We would tailor Coworker to the way your teams work with skills: reusable playbooks that standardize common workflows, reporting methods and analysis approaches, so nobody has to explain the same process again.

You keep control through approval gates, permissions inherited from your Adobe organization, checks before actions run and an audit trail. Skills do not store customer data: data access stays governed through your connected Adobe applications, permissions and organizational controls.
Coworker acts across Adobe and external systems through governed access, using built-in connectors or your own. An external tool or service is connected by adding it as a server.
As Coworker takes on a task you can watch it reason and progress. It validates the results and brings the finished work back to you for approval.

Firefly Creative Production is Adobe's enterprise offering for scaled content automation. It brings together workflow authoring, headless creative services and a production runtime to produce on-brand outputs at scale, for work such as campaign variants, localization and templated asset production.
Firefly Creative Production produces on-brand outputs at scale through reusable workflows.

We would turn your existing production playbook into reusable workflows: define the inputs, assemble the steps, add logic and test the flow, then link it to your source systems, review tools and storage locations so that it fits into your existing environment.

The Workflow API executes published workflows across multiple assets in one batch. Your external platforms can trigger workflow executions, with processed outputs returned to the originating environment, and Firefly Services APIs cover headless and programmatic use cases.

Your admin assigns access in the Admin Console. Workflow authoring and admin access can stay with a smaller group of specialists, while a broader group runs the published workflows, guided experiences, APIs or bulk actions.

Teams monitor progress and review results on each run, focusing attention on exceptions rather than on every asset. The Workflow API returns batch status with asset counts, execution statistics and estimated time remaining.

Firefly Custom Models let you train Firefly generative models on your own images, so generated content reflects a specific visual style or subject. The models are private by default and designed for commercial use.
Firefly Custom Models generate content in your own visual style or of your own subject.

Training a custom model has three key actions: upload, analyze and train. We would prepare the images with you, review the captions, tags and recommendations Firefly generates for the training dataset, and confirm that you have the rights to use the uploaded images.

A subject model makes generated images consistently represent a particular object, character or product; a style model makes them share visual characteristics such as color, texture and lighting. Brand colors can be defined before training to help maintain color consistency.
A system administrator entitles the people who train models. Models are private by default, and publishing and sharing are managed through Custom Model projects.
Trained models can be used to generate content in supported Adobe apps, including Photoshop, Illustrator, Adobe Express, Firefly and GenStudio.

Brand Intelligence is a continuously learning platform that helps your teams create and validate on-brand content. It learns from your assets, past reviews and team decisions, and is a headless platform exposed through APIs rather than a separate app.
Brand Intelligence checks whether content adheres to your brand standards before it goes live.

Brand Intelligence brings together your brand guidelines, design systems, creative assets, human feedback and approvals, and your brand profile is configured during onboarding. Because it is a headless platform exposed through APIs, we would then integrate it with your existing apps.

The Validate skill automatically checks whether content adheres to your brand standards before it goes live, across designs, images, documents and layouts. Each approval, edit or rejection of a suggestion feeds back into Brand Intelligence for continuous learning.
The Instruct to Assemble skill turns a campaign brief into on-brand content variants by selecting the best-fit creative elements and assembling them into production-ready outputs.

It integrates through APIs: your systems submit a batch of assets and receive structured pass/fail feedback per asset, authenticated with OAuth Server-to-Server credentials set up in the Adobe Developer Console.

confirm.text: Brand Concierge region: Adobe's FAQ says personal data from a conversation "stays local in line with applicable regional regulations", and Adobe's March 2026 security overview says every part runs in US-East. It stays out of the response until Adobe says which is current.

Brand Concierge and AI training: Adobe's FAQ says it is "specifically trained on your organization's content and customer data", and the March 2026 security overview says "Adobe does not use customer data to train Brand Concierge". It stays out of the response until Adobe says which is current.
Experience Platform regions: Adobe's pages list them differently (India as IND1 or IND2; Switzerland only on the Customer Journey Analytics page). Confirm the region your client needs is offered.

Experience Platform on AWS: Adobe says it is "currently available to a limited number of customers". The response names AWS as an option Adobe offers, not a promise; confirm it with Adobe if your client needs AWS.
Target hosting: Adobe's page says both "Adobe-owned and Adobe-leased data centers" and "hosted on AWS". The response names only the cluster cities.
Marketo data center: Adobe's page still lists some subscriptions as moving to AWS. Confirm your client's data center and pod.

FedRAMP and IRAP on Adobe's Trust Center list cover named offerings only: FedRAMP Tailored applies to Adobe Analytics and Adobe Campaign, FedRAMP Moderate to AEM Gov Cloud and Connect Gov Cloud, and IRAP to Customer Journey Analytics Australia and AEM Gov Cloud Australia at Protected Level. The response leaves them out; name one only if your client is on that offering.
Workfront cluster: Adobe's pages list the EU clusters differently and still describe a move to AWS for some clusters. Confirm your client's cluster.
Commerce App Builder storage: Adobe's Commerce security page says there is no encryption of data kept in App Builder storage. Check whether the build uses it.
Coworker: Adobe's Workfront pages say Coworker is not currently available to organizations in health care, finance or some other industries with sensitive data. Confirm your client is eligible.

asks.text: Which region your client's data must stay in. The region is chosen at setup and cannot be moved later.
asks.client: The region your data must stay in, since the region is chosen at setup and cannot be moved later.

asks.text: Which identity provider your client's team signs in with, such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID.
asks.client: The identity provider your team signs in with, such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID.

asks.text: The uptime and recovery targets your client needs.
asks.client: The uptime and recovery targets you need.

asks.text: The consent management platform your client uses, if any.
asks.client: The consent management platform you use, if any.
